title: The ILS in Plain English
hook: Two needles, one runway, zero visibility. Meet the ILS.

scenes.narration: Vectors to final, ceiling three hundred overcast, three-quarters of a mile. The controller says: cleared I L S two-seven, maintain two thousand until established. Two needles between you and the pavement, kid.
Three hundred overcast. A standard I L S goes down to what height above the touchdown zone? Commit to a number.
Two hundred feet — and as little as a half mile. So your three hundred overcast? Workable. Two beams get you there: localizer for left-right, glideslope for the three-degree slide down.
onScreenText: Standard CAT I: 200 ft & ½ SM

scenes.narration: The localizer is four times touchier than a V O R. Why? The beam narrows to runway width — the precision comes from the geometry, and it bites hardest near the ground. Pressure, not heroics.
At two hundred feet you decide. Runway environment — land. Nothing? Missed, now. The glideslope does not care about your dinner reservation.
Eyes off the screen. The two beams, the two numbers, and what happens at D A. Out loud.
Localizer left-right. Glideslope down. Two hundred and a half. Decide at D A. Saving bacon since before I had this mustache.
From the briefing lesson — the last two items of the brief, the ones you say out loud. Go.
A I M one dash one dash nine. Every beam, marker, and mile. Bring coffee.

quiz.question: Ceiling 300 overcast, ¾ SM. A standard Category I ILS bottoms out at:
choices: DA 200 ft HAT, visibility ½ SM / RVR 1,800
quiz.explanation: A standard CAT I ILS goes down to 200 ft above touchdown with as little as ½ SM or RVR 1,800 — so 300 overcast is workable. (AIM 1-1-9; exact values on the plate)

quiz.question: Compared to a VOR course, the localizer is:
choices: About 4x more sensitive — small corrections only
quiz.explanation: The localizer's full-scale deflection is roughly a quarter of a VOR's, so needle movements are faster — correct with small pressures.

quiz.question: Reaching DA without the runway environment in sight, you must:
choices: Level off at DA and continue to the MAP
quiz.explanation: DA is a decision altitude — no runway environment means missed approach, beginning at DA. (91.175)
